text: dsh-git-flow 是 DSH 网页客户端的工作区 Git 管理插件。它在对话输入区工具栏加入当前分支状态入口，并通过主机 API 操作会话对应工作区。用户可以浏览、搜索、切换和创建分支，执行合并、变基、抓取、推送、重命名和删除，也能勾选文件提交并生成 AI 提交信息；另提供 feature、release、hotfix 的 git-flow 开始与完成流程。适合在 DSH 网页会话中直接管理项目版本控制的开发者。需要本机工作区为 Git 仓库并可调用 git；提交信息使用会话已选模型。

dsh-git-flow adds Git branch controls to DSH web conversations: browse, switch, create, merge, rebase, fetch, push, rename and delete branches. Users can commit selected files with a session-model drafted message and run feature, release or hotfix flows. Requires git in the workspace host.
我想直接在 DSH 对话里查看和切换项目分支。
能不能从界面新建一个 Git 分支并切过去？
让 DSH 帮我把选中的文件提交，并起草提交说明。
我想在分支菜单里合并、变基或推送代码。
I want to manage Git branches from my DSH conversation.
Can I commit only the files I selected and get a drafted message?
I need a visual way to start and finish feature or release branches.
dsh-git-flow 的功能「分支管理」：在会话工具栏打开分支菜单，浏览和搜索本地及远程分支，并切换、新建、合并、变基、抓取、推送、重命名或删除分支。
dsh-git-flow 的功能「勾选提交」：提交面板列出工作区变更，用户勾选文件并提交；服务只将选中的路径纳入提交，也可选择随后推送。
dsh-git-flow 的功能「AI 提交信息」：在提交面板请求草拟提交信息，服务使用该会话记录的模型路由根据变更生成 conventional commit 格式文本；模型不可用时提供模板回退。
dsh-git-flow 的功能「git-flow 分支」：通过界面开始或完成 feature、release、hotfix 分支；完成 release 或 hotfix 时按配置合并回目标分支并处理版本与标签。
如何在 DSH 里查看工作区改了哪些文件并提交其中一部分？

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · dsh-git-flow：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A DeepSeek Harness workspace git plugin: a branch chip in the composer tool row. Open it to browse branches, switch branches, create one, merge one into the current branch, and commit a checked subset of files — the commit message is written by the session's own model from the diff.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · dsh-git-flow：```
composer tool row:  [⑂ feature/login  3]  ← click (a Feature badge sits beside it)
                      ├ Search branches
                      ├ Local branches · 2   ✓ feature/login
                      │                        main
@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Install：Two ways in; either one is enough.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · From the plugin page (GUI)：The GitHub address `https://github.com/hunan36/dsh-git-flow` also works, but `pnpm` pins the dependency to that commit and will not follow new releases. Installing by package name is what makes version comparison and updates possible.

**Restart `dsh web`** afterwards: host-half changes are not hot-reloaded, and the browser fetches the new client bundle on restart.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Updating：DSH does not auto-update third-party plugins; updating takes one command:

```bash
pnpm --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/web add @hunan36/dsh-git-flow@latest
```

Then **restart `dsh web`**. Host-half changes (services and API routes) only apply after a restart; the browser half refetches its bundle then.

Check the installed and latest versions:

```bash
npm view @hunan36/dsh-git-flow version
```

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Updating：Installs by GitHub address are not followed automatically (`pnpm` pinned a commit), so reinstall explicitly to update:

```bash
pnpm --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/web add github:hunan36/dsh-git-flow#main
```

text: @hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · or: corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate：Both need one extra step: add `@hunan36/dsh-git-flow` to that profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` in its `package.json`, then restart `dsh web`. The plugin page and `dsh plugin add` do that for you; a manual install does not, and the package stays unloaded even though it sits in `node_modules`.

text:
@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Point the plugin page at npm (a machine that only has npm)：The plugin page runs `pnpm add <spec>` by default, but the plugin manager's command is configurable — set it to `npm` in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and the page installs with npm:

```yaml
section: Point the plugin page at npm (a machine that only has npm)

text:
@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml：- id: plugin-manager
  config:
    pnpmCommand: npm
```

Then use the plugin page exactly as usual (paste the address → Install → Enable). The CLI's `dsh plugin … add` does **not** honour this setting and still needs pnpm.

Three caveats:

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Installation fails with ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT：A dsh profile directory is itself a pnpm workspace (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` with `packages: [.]`), and pnpm 8 treats `pnpm add` there as adding to a workspace root — which it refuses. When the profile has no `packageManager` field, Node's Corepack fills one in (commonly `pnpm@8.15.7`), and the install then dies on that check **before it ever resolves this plugin**, so the failure is not about this package.

Any one of these gets you through:

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Installation fails with ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT：1. **Installing from the plugin page (GUI)**: that path runs `pnpm add <spec>` and cannot pass `-w`, so do step 2 first (write the `.npmrc`) and then press "Retry" in the dialog — the same command then succeeds under pnpm 8.
2. Teach the profile to accept a root dependency, then install exactly as documented:

```bash
   echo 'ignore-workspace-root-check=true' >> ~/.dsh/profiles/gitflow-web/.npmrc
   ```

3. From the CLI, pass `-w` through (dsh forwards extra arguments to pnpm):

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Installation fails with ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT：```bash
   dsh plugin --profile gitflow-web add -w https://github.com/hunan36/dsh-git-flow.git
   ```

4. Put the profile on pnpm 10 (the version this plugin is tested with): run `corepack use pnpm@10` in the profile, or set the `packageManager` field Corepack added to `pnpm@10.22.0`.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Installation fails with ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT：Note that after the first failure Corepack has already written `packageManager: pnpm@8.15.7+sha512…` into that profile's `package.json`, so every later plugin operation there uses pnpm 8 — step 4 is the durable fix.

Requires Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` and pnpm 10; this repository pins it with `packageManager: pnpm@10.22.0`.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `timeoutMs` | 15000 | Deadline for read-only and local git commands |
| `pushTimeoutMs` | 120000 | Deadline for `git push`, which waits on a remote |
| `messageMaxDiffBytes` | 65536 | Cap on the diff bytes handed to the model (truncated past it) |
| `messageLanguage` | `en` | Default commit-message language, `zh` or `en` |
| `productionBranch` | `main` | Production branch name; set `master` for older repos |
| `developBranch` | `develop` | Integration branch name |
| `featurePrefix` | `feature/` | Feature branch prefix |
| `releasePrefix` | `release/` | Release branch prefix |
| `hotfixPrefix` | `hotfix/` | Hotfix branch prefix |
| `tagPrefix` | `v` | Tag prefix applied when a release or hotfix finishes |

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Configuration：The commit panel carries an `English | 中文` switch beside "Draft message". It overrides `messageLanguage` for that call and remembers the choice in `localStorage`, so English stays the default until you pick otherwise.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Merging a branch：Right-click a branch row (or press the keyboard menu key / `Shift+F10` while it is focused) to get the branch actions below. This section
covers checkout and merge; rebase, fetch, push, rename, delete, and copy live in [Branch actions](#branch-actions).

- **Checkout** — the same switch as a left click, including the dirty-worktree confirmation.
- **Merge into the current branch** — runs `git merge --no-edit <branch>` on the current branch; nothing is pushed.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Merging a branch：A merge that can fast-forward does; a diverged branch produces a normal merge commit with git's default message. The toast reports which happened. A remote-only row merges its `origin/…` ref without creating a local branch.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Merging a branch：A conflict is **not** aborted: the conflict markers, the index and `MERGE_HEAD` stay in the worktree, and the chip starts showing the conflicted files. Resolve them and commit the merge yourself — from a terminal or by asking the session. The commit panel only makes partial commits (`git commit --only`), which git refuses while a merge is in progress. If local edits would be overwritten, the merge fails with `git/dirty-worktree` and the worktree is left untouched. Merging the current branch into itself and merging into a detached HEAD are both refused.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Branch actions：The same right-click menu covers the rest of SourceTree's local-branch actions. They act on the **selected** branch (except rebase, which always replays the current branch onto the selected one):

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Branch actions：| Action | What it runs |
|---|---|
| Rebase current changes onto `<branch>` | `git rebase <branch>` — the current branch's commits are replayed on top of it, so its history is rewritten |
| Fetch `<branch>` | `git fetch <remote>` for the branch's remote; a remote-only row fetches its own remote |
| Push to `<upstream>` (tracked) | `git push <remote> <branch>:<tracked branch>` for that branch |
| Push to… | pick a remote and a destination branch: `git push --set-upstream <remote> <branch>:<destination>` |
| Rename… | `git branch -m` for a local branch (the upstream config moves with it) |
| Delete `<branch>` | `git branch -d`; a not-fully-merged branch asks for confirmation and retries with `-D` |
| Copy branch name | copies the name to the clipboard |

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Git flow：The bottom two rows of the branch menu start and finish standard git-flow branches: features and releases branch off `develop`,
hotfixes branch off production, and a finish merges back with `--no-ff`.

| Type | Branches off | Merges into | Tag + version bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `feature/` | `develop` | `develop` | no |
| `release/` | `develop` | production + `develop` | yes |
| `hotfix/` | production | production + `develop` | yes |
@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Git flow：A finish runs: merge, tag, commit the `package.json` `version`, push the branches and tag, delete the local branch.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Git flow：- When `develop` does not exist yet, "Start" offers to create it from production (or the current branch).
- Merges, tags, and version commits are not rolled back; a failed push reports "finished locally, but the push failed" and keeps the local result.
- Everything that can be refused is checked before the first write: a dirty worktree, an existing tag, a missing target branch.
- A merge conflict is left in place for you to resolve; nothing is aborted on your behalf.
- A repository without a root `package.json` skips the version step instead of failing.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Security boundaries：- The browser sends only a `sessionId`. The host resolves the repository from that session's workspace, so a page can never name a directory for git to run in.
- Arguments are always an array, never a shell string, with `stdin: 'ignore'` and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, so a credential prompt can never hang a call.
- `push` never passes `--force` or `--force-with-lease`, and only pushes the current branch's upstream (with `--set-upstream <remote> HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` when it has none).
- Commits stage only the files checked in the panel. An empty selection answers `git/no-files-selected` and never falls back to an implicit `git add -A`.
- A merge runs only `git merge --no-edit <name>` against the current branch, with a branch name the browser sent. It never passes `--no-ff`/`--force`/`-X`, never pushes, and never aborts a conflicted merge.
- Branch actions run exactly one fixed git subcommand each: `git rebase <branch>`, `git fetch <remote>`, `git push <remote> <branch>:refs/heads/<dest>`, `git branch -m <from> <to>`, `git branch -d|-D <branch>`. Remote names are only accepted when they appear in `git remote`; fetch never prunes o

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Layout：```
src/
├── index.ts       host entry (default-exports the GitFlow service)
├── service.ts     GitFlow: status / branches / checkout / createBranch / merge / rebase / fetch / push / pushBranch /
│                  renameBranch / deleteBranch / remotes / commit / discard / pull / generateMessage

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Build：```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build       # tsc -> lib/types/**, tsdown -> lib/index.js + lib/client.js
```

**`lib/` is committed to the repository** (it is not in `.gitignore`) and the package no longer carries a `prepare` script, so installing from the git URL needs no build, no dev dependencies, and no entry in pnpm's `onlyBuiltDependencies` allowlist:

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Build：- `lib/index.js`: Node ESM, imported directly by the cordis loader.
- `lib/client.js`: a CJS factory wrapped as `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: "@hunan36/dsh-git-flow", factory: (require) => … })` (the id is `package.json`'s `name`); `react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` stay external and come from the page's static module table.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Compatibility：Developed and verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.6-alpha.2`, with peer and dev dependencies pinned to it. dsh is still alpha, so contracts such as `conversation.input.left`, `ctx.webServer.register`, and `ctx.slots.inject` may drift between minor versions. After upgrading dsh, rebuild and confirm the first line of `lib/client.js` is still `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: "@hunan36/dsh-git-flow"`.

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Known limits：- An AI commit message needs one turn already sent in the session (the provider/model recorded in `request/header`). Without a route the panel answers `git/no-route` and tells you to send one message first; when the model fails or returns nothing usable, the `chore: update N files` template fills in and says so.
- Messages default to English. The panel's language switch (remembered per browser) and the `messageLanguage` config are the only two inputs; the template fallback follows the same choice.
- Remote branches appear only once `refs/remotes/**` exists locally (the plugin never fetches in the background); "Refresh status" makes no network call.
- Conflicted files cannot be checked; resolve the conflict in the conversation first.
- `git switch --force` discards **all** local changes, not just the conflicting ones — the confirmation copy says exactly that. To drop a single file's changes instead, use that file's Discard action in the commit panel.
- Switching to a ref that exists nowhere fails inside git and is reported as `git/failed` with git's own text. Only stale UI state can reach that path, since the menu lists branches that exist

@hunan36/dsh-git-flow README · Verification (0.1.6-alpha.2)：Measured on an isolated `DSH_HOME` with profile `gitflow-web` (`@hunan36/dsh-git-flow` appended to `dsh.profile.bundles`): the chip text equals `git branch --show-current`; the menu lists every local branch plus each remote-only one; search filters rows; switching moves both the chip and the worktree files; a dirty switch is refused and only confirms `--force` after a second dialog; an invalid branch name errors while a valid one is created and switched to; with a single file checked, the model returned a `feat: …` message and `git log -1 --name-only` showed only that file; commit-and-push made the branch appear in `git ls-remote` with its upstream set; a session whose workspace is not a repository renders no chip; the `headless` profile boots with no warning and no routes.
